definitions.explanation: a person devoted to study and learning, especially in an academic or scholarly context

examples.japanese: {学徒|がくと}{動員|どういん}で{多|おお}くの{若者|わかもの}が{戦場|せんじょう}に{送|おく}られた。
examples.english: Many young people were sent to the battlefield through student mobilization.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{法学|ほうがく}の{学徒|がくと}として{研鑽|けんさん}を{積|つ}んだ。
examples.english: He trained diligently as a student of law.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}き{学徒|がくと}たちが{新|あたら}しい{時代|じだい}の{学問|がくもん}を{切|き}り{開|ひら}いていった。
examples.english: Young scholars pioneered new fields of study for a new era.

notes:
A formal and somewhat literary word for students or scholars. Most strongly associated with the historical term {学徒|がくと}{動員|どういん} (student mobilization), which refers to the conscription of university students into military service during World War II.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {学徒|がくと}{動員|どういん}: student mobilization (WWII term)
- {学徒|がくと}{出陣|しゅつじん}: students going off to war
- {法学|ほうがく}の{学徒|がくと}: student of law

ETYMOLOGY:
{学徒|がくと}{動員|どういん} (1943-1945) was a wartime policy that drafted university and higher school students into factories and eventually into combat. It remains a significant topic in Japanese war history and is frequently referenced in historical discussions and memorials.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {学生|がくせい}: student — the standard modern word for a student
- {生徒|せいと}: pupil, student — used mainly for secondary school students
- {学者|がくしゃ}: scholar — an established academic or researcher
